identification: @serifpersia/dango 3.7.4: Node CLI/server and React anime/media application

decisive_diff.changes: 108 members in both releases; 55 same-name members byte-identical, 49 assets renamed by content hashes, four same-name manifest/document/HTML changes. After pairing exact filenames first and normalizing local identifiers, asset hashes and CSS-module labels, 43 changed JavaScript files have identical token streams. The remaining JavaScript changes are the MediaCard horizontal CSS export and the frontend version string. CSS changes concern layout. Settings token helper is byte-identical.
decisive_diff.queue_caveat: The supplied guidance says an earlier release had no detections. Recovered immediately preceding 3.7.3 fires the same suspicious bookmarklet and 778 notable traits under the current pre-edit rules; the observed change is not introduction of credential theft.

behavior_trace: CLI parses mode/ports, checks the Node version, offers an interactive npm update, spawns its local server/client, and authenticates local shutdown using a random token. No install hook is declared.

Settings generates a javascript: bookmarklet using encodeURIComponent. The user drags/copies it to a bookmark and invokes it on discord.com. It traverses webpack module exports and calls getToken(), writes that token to clipboard using writeText or a temporary textarea/execCommand copy, then closes the tab. It has no network send. The instructions explicitly describe copying the token and require manual paste/save.

The Save click passes the password-input state to discord.gatewaySave.mutate through the same-origin /api/trpc client. The backend trims the token, persists DISCORD_GATEWAY_TOKEN in the application data .env, reloads the gateway service, and returns a masked value. The service authenticates to wss://gateway.discord.gg and calls Discord external-assets API for Rich Presence. The UI discloses Discord Terms-of-Service/account suspension risks.

Google sync loads its own google_tokens.json, obtains user authorization, exchanges the callback code, refreshes expiring tokens and issues authenticated Drive requests for application snapshots. By default code/refresh grants go through the publisher worker. The separately retrieved current repository main declares version 3.7.4; its published worker forwards grants to oauth2.googleapis.com/token using the server-held client secret and returns the token response, without a storage or extra transfer operation. Live read-only /auth-url points to accounts.google.com with localhost callback and drive.appdata, drive.file, userinfo.email consent scopes.

Remote media providers are loaded from the publisher registry, checked against declared SHA-256 before caching and dynamic import, and validated for the provider interface. This extensibility is a mutable trust dependency; it does not establish compromise in the supplied bytes.

Minification is ordinary bundler output. The bookmarklet is plaintext source encoded only when its link is generated. Decoded-string inspection found no encoded strings in Settings; server decoded candidates include escaped bundled library/source runs and data tables, not a concealed execution chain.
remaining_context: Live worker implementation and log retention cannot be proven from published source; future mutable provider content and actual LAN exposure/user authorization are unknown. No deployment circumstance is invented.

external_disagreement.claim: LPM calls the publisher-worker OAuth relay credential exfiltration without recipient-specific consent.
external_disagreement.assessment: The transfer is real and remains covered by notable OAuth token-body, refresh-grant and HTTP traits. Its role in the explicit Google synchronization workflow, published secret-holding broker, normal consent response and unchanged server favors benign intent. Incomplete UI disclosure is not evidence of compromise by itself.

trait_correction.unsupported_claim: A bare case-insensitive providerOrder word was treated as the NetworkProvider registry value; the actual match destructures a media-provider preference list.
trait_correction.fix: Require a standalone extracted string, quoted value name or explicit PowerShell -Name / reg.exe /v value argument. Retain notable severity, Windows/source scopes, standalone binary-string coverage, and existing consumers. Description now states the matched evidence.
trait_correction.consumer_audit: Only two composites explicitly reference the atom, both in network-provider.yaml. Other registry directory references were inspected. No pre-existing ProviderOrder fixtures were found.
trait_correction.retained_dual_use: discord-webpack-token-clipboard-grab remains suspicious, including on the archive parent.

verification.focused_checks: PASS: six cases: real PSBits registration and audit sources, Python quoted registry value, reg.exe unquoted value, JavaScript provider-list near miss, and value-name suffix/bare-variable near miss.
verification.real_positive_preservation: Every (trait ID, severity) on upstream PSBits ConfigureRegistrySettings.ps1 is identical before and after. Both direct consumers still fire.
verification.material_attack_detection_losses: None. Only the erroneous registry-name finding is lost, on Player-hVrgi0J1.js and its archive parent. All hostile/suspicious and all other notable detections are unchanged.
verification.analysis_limits: Scanner records flow-budget limitations in bundled JavaScript; relevant paths were inspected statically instead of inferring safety from scan coverage.
